The user has just given a very extensive set of UI redesign requirements: an orange‑themed overhaul with three new modes (Discord, Search, Fun Fact) and various interactive features. They’re essentially asking for a complete redesign and addition of substantial functionality. However, I have no visibility into the existing codebase—what framework it uses (React, Streamlit, Gradio?), how the UI is currently structured, what components exist, and how data (chat history, user messages) is stored and accessed. Jumping straight into design or implementation without that context would be reckless; I could suggest changes that conflict with the current architecture, miss key integration points, or duplicate existing functionality.

My next logical step must be to examine the current source files. By looking at the repository, I can identify the main UI entry point, styling conventions, state management, and any existing hooks for fetching chat history. This will also reveal whether there’s already a theming system I can extend with the orange palette, and whether the app already supports mode switching that I could repurpose. Knowing the data flow will be crucial for implementing the Discord‑style read‑only view, the real‑time search highlighting, and the statistical analysis for the Fun Fact mode.

Given that the user hasn’t provided any code snippets or a file list, the safest and most constructive response is to ask them to show the current UI code (or point me to the relevant files). That way I can base any redesign proposals on the actual implementation rather than on assumptions.

Therefore, I’ll respond succinctly, prompting the user to share the current code so I can start the analysis.
